raw_response:
I've been farming these 3 mu in Quzhou for 30 years, and at 50 I know what works on this land. With only 3 mu for a family of four, and some of my people working off-farm, I can't afford to gamble. I keep 2 mu in the wheat-maize double crop because that's my food security and feed base — the North China Plain was made for this rotation. I plant improved wheat in October, and as soon as it's out in early June, I put in hybrid maize. That June window is narrow, so I don't till for the maize — I plant no-till to save every day I can. The other 1 mu goes to hybrid Bt cotton. Cotton brings cash for school and daily costs, but it's hand-labor intensive for planting, thinning, spraying, and picking, so 1 mu is my limit given that part of my household is away working. My well gives me water when the rains fail. For wheat, I'll irrigate three times — green-up, jointing, and grain filling. For summer maize, twice is usually enough with the summer rains — jointing and filling. Cotton is thirsty at flowering and boll-set, so three irrigations there. I fertilize with compound base and urea top-dress: wheat gets about 16-7-4 NPK per mu, maize gets 16-5-5, and cotton needs more potassium for its bolls so 13-6-9. Wheat and maize each need two pesticide passes, but cotton is a pest magnet even with Bt, so I budget four sprays.
